output_list.reason: The 'distributeToken' function has an integer overflow attack vulnerability. When _value is large, the 'balances[msg.sender] -= _value' statement can cause the token amount of the attackers becomes infinite aka 'broken' due to underflow.

The 'transfer' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When _value is large, the 'balances[msg.sender] -= _value' statement can cause a 'world' state variable becomes extremely large due to underflow.

The 'transferFrom' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When _value is large, the 'balances[_from] -= _value' statement can cause an attacker's contract's balance becomes extremely large and unusable due to underflow.
The 'distributeToken' function has incorrect access control. It allows anyone to distribute tokens, aka 'world' writable state variables.
The 'B2X' contract defines a constructor with a typo, it is 'function B2X()' instead of 'constructor()' due to misspelled identifier 'constructor'.
